Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Creative Group Facilitator, Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,
I recently came across your Creative Group Facilitator opening and wanted to introduce myself. I understand the position may have been filled, but I would welcome consideration for this or future opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My background brings together adolescent behavioral health support, recovery group facilitation, visual arts education, and fitness and wellness programming. 

At Family Center for Recovery, I supported adolescents and adults in structured treatment settings. At Futures Recovery Healthcare, I facilitated recovery support groups and helped alumni connect with resources and coping strategies. More recently, as an art teacher, I have designed creative activities that encourage confidence, expression, and engagement.

I am especially drawn to opportunities to help young people strengthen self-esteem and positive self-talk through art, movement, drama-inspired expression, and mindfulness. My approach values practical DBT-informed skills and creative activities as complements to the work of licensed treatment professionals.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience might support your programming. I have attached my resume for your consideration. 

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards, Jennifer Winston

candidates.cover_letter:
Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

October 26, 2026

Hiring Committee
Launch AWA NC
Re: Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health position with Launch AWA NC. As a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with more than 25 years of experience in clinical and child-and-family services, including over 15 years in program and clinical leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise, operational management, staff development, and a strong commitment to improving outcomes for children, adolescents, and families. I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. I value collaborative leadership, clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and creating an environment where clinicians feel supported in their work and equipped to provide the highest quality of care.

Throughout my career, I have remained committed to serving children and families, particularly those impacted by trauma and other significant life challenges. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my experience to Launch AWA NC and help strengthen mental health services for adolescents. Given my extensive experience, clinical background, and leadership responsibilities, I would also welcome a conversation about compensation. I recognize that the position has a posted salary range; however, I am seeking compensation above that range that more fully reflects my qualifications and the value I would bring to the role. I hope there may be flexibility to discuss a package that aligns with my experience and the position’s responsibilities.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, leadership experience, and commitment to serving adolescents and families could contribute to the continued success of Launch AWA NC.

Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

November 2, 2026

Re: Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than 20 years of experience in behavioral health and social services, including outpatient program management, staff supervision, residential operations, and regulatory compliance, I believe my background aligns well with the day-to-day leadership and organizational needs of your adolescent PHP/IOP program.
Throughout my career, I have helped coordinate intakes, staff and interdisciplinary services, treatment planning, documentation review, and quality improvement. I understand the importance of maintaining a structured, safe environment while ensuring that team members have clear expectations, clients receive consistent support, and services remain aligned with policies and regulatory requirements. I have also worked with individuals experiencing mental health and co-occurring substance use challenges, where a calm response, effective communication, and sound judgment are essential.
Although much of my recent experience has been with adults, my earlier work providing ABA services gave me experience with structured behavioral interventions and individualized support. I would bring that foundation, along with a person-centered and trauma-informed approach, to working collaboratively with your wellness coordinators, clinical team, adolescents, and families. I value compassion, dignity, respect, and accountability, and I believe those qualities are equally important in leading staff and supporting clients.
I hold the Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager Supervisor (CBHCMS) credential and am completing my Master of Social Work at Walden University, with degree conferral anticipated in November 2026. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my operations and leadership experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and help support a consistent, high-quality program experience.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience aligns with your team’s needs.

Sincerely,
 
Michelle Antonia Rivera

Re: Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Behavioral Health

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Program Operations Manager – Adolescent Behavioral Health position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over ten years of experience in behavioral health, youth services, case management, and program operations, along with a Master’s degree in Psychological Counseling, I offer a strong combination of operational leadership, staff development, crisis management, and a commitment to creating safe, structured, and supportive environments for adolescents and families.

In my current role as Associate Regional Director with Compass Connections, I oversee specialized case management operations across more than six states in the Midwest region, supervising up to eight professionals and overseeing workloads involving up to 120 cases. My responsibilities include staff recruitment, performance evaluations, case assignments, quality assurance, training, and operational coordination. I was promoted into regional leadership within three months of joining the organization, reflecting my ability to take initiative, manage competing priorities, and lead with accountability.

My experience as Lead Case Manager at Homestead Emergency Influx Shelter further prepared me to lead teams serving vulnerable youth. I supervised 18 Case Managers supporting approximately 50 unaccompanied minors, coordinating services, reviewing documentation, supporting family reunification, and maintaining compliance with federal program requirements. This role strengthened my ability to respond calmly to complex situations while prioritizing safety, clear communication, and consistent service delivery.

Additionally, as Director of Teen Challenge International, I managed daily program operations, supervised 40 employees and volunteers, oversaw services for 50 participants, and coordinated staffing, facilities, resources, and administrative processes. My background in psychological counseling and family services has also equipped me to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary professionals and support individuals experiencing emotional, behavioral, and family-related challenges.

What attracts me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to combine operational excellence with meaningful service to adolescents and families. I understand the importance of maintaining structured routines, supporting staff through clear expectations and coaching, ensuring accurate documentation, and working closely with clinical leadership to provide a consistent and compassionate experience.

As a bilingual professional fluent in English and Spanish, I would bring strong communication skills, cultural awareness, and a collaborative leadership approach to your team. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience can contribute to the effectiveness, safety, and continued success of your adolescent behavioral health programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

Magdiel Alejandro Ramos

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With experience in behavioral health coordination, client communication, scheduling, and administrative support, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of creating a welcoming and supportive experience for individuals seeking care. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it would allow me to build on my current experience in mental health services while helping individuals and families navigate the admissions process and take meaningful steps toward treatment.

In my current role as a Client Care Coordinator at Cambridge Mental Health, I work directly with clients, clinicians, and other providers to coordinate services and support continuity of care. My responsibilities include helping clients navigate mental health services, coordinating referrals and treatment-related appointments, communicating with providers, maintaining confidential records, and assisting with intake and follow-up processes. I also serve as a primary point of contact at the front desk, where I regularly field questions from clients, families, and clinicians. This experience has strengthened my ability to communicate with compassion, respond to sensitive situations professionally, and help individuals feel supported while navigating what can sometimes be an overwhelming healthcare system. I am also familiar with Kipu and behavioral health intake processes, and I understand the importance of accurate documentation and timely communication throughout the admissions process.

In addition to my behavioral health experience, I bring practical experience working remotely and independently. My current position includes numerous remote workdays, during which I am responsible for managing scheduling, coordinating communication, completing administrative tasks, and maintaining follow-through without the immediate presence of an in-person team. This has strengthened my ability to stay organized, manage competing priorities, and remain responsive and accountable while working independently. I am comfortable balancing phone and administrative responsibilities while ensuring that clients and providers receive timely assistance.

My experience has also allowed me to develop strong organizational and follow-through skills through managing appointments, coordinating referrals, maintaining records, and helping connect clients with appropriate providers and community resources. I understand that admissions coordination requires more than simply scheduling appointments; it requires listening carefully, identifying individual needs, communicating next steps clearly, and ensuring that people do not feel lost during the process. I would bring that same level of care and attention to individuals and families reaching out to your programs.

With bachelor's degrees in Psychology and English from Mount Holyoke College, I bring an academic foundation in human behavior, communication, and interpersonal relationships alongside my practical experience in behavioral health services. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team by combining my knowledge of mental health coordination, familiarity with intake processes and Kipu, and ability to work independently in a remote environment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and commitment to client-centered care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Parker McDuffee

Kayla Gillin
Riverview, Florida
813-614-2352

November 9, 2026

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I have several years of healthcare experience, including working directly with children and adolescents experiencing mental health challenges. I will also be graduating from St. Petersburg College on December 14, 2026, with my Bachelor’s degree in Human Services. I believe my education, professional experience, and passion for helping others would make me a great addition to your team.

In my previous role as a Mental Health Patient Care Technician at St. Joseph’s Children’s Hospital, I worked closely with children and adolescents experiencing mental health crises, behavioral challenges, and various psychiatric disorders. Many of the patients I encountered had complex backgrounds, including experiences in group homes, difficult family situations, and underlying mental health conditions. Through this experience, I developed a deeper understanding of how important it is to connect with these individuals beyond their diagnosis or current circumstances. I made it a priority to build rapport with my patients, understand their behaviors, and create an environment where they felt comfortable, respected, and supported.

One of the things I am particularly proud of is creating a pediatric behavioral health report sheet to improve communication between staff members during patient handoffs. I recognized that caring for behavioral health patients should involve more than simply observing them throughout a 12 hour shift. My goal was to help staff better understand each patient’s background, behaviors, emotional needs, potential triggers, and any history of self harming behaviors or statements. Having this information readily available helped support more meaningful patient interactions, improved continuity of care, and provided valuable observations that could be communicated to psychiatrists, behavioral health therapists, and other members of the treatment team.

Working with these patients gave me a genuine appreciation for the challenges children and adolescents face when dealing with mental health conditions. I learned that building trust, listening without judgment, and taking the time to understand someone’s experiences can make a significant difference in how they respond to care. This experience strengthened my communication skills, patience, compassion, and ability to work with individuals during some of their most vulnerable moments.

In addition to my behavioral health experience, my previous role as a NICU Nurse Technician at Tampa General Hospital strengthened my ability to remain organized, communicate effectively with families, maintain accurate documentation, and work collaboratively with healthcare professionals. My education in Human Services and my 180 hour internship have also expanded my knowledge of mental health, community resources, and connecting individuals and families with appropriate services.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an emotional and overwhelming experience for both adolescents and their families. I would love the opportunity to use my background to help families feel comfortable, informed, and supported throughout the admissions process. I believe my ability to connect with people, understand their concerns, and approach difficult situations with empathy would allow me to make a positive impact in this position.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to further discuss how my experience, education, and dedication to supporting children and families align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Kayla Gillin

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a professional background in behavioral health, care coordination, substance use counseling, and healthcare administration, I am confident in my ability to provide compassionate, organized, and effective support to individuals and families seeking treatment.

In my current role as a Care Coordinator and Substance Use Counselor at Intermountain Centers, I work closely with adolescents, families, healthcare providers, and community agencies to coordinate behavioral health services and ensure individuals receive appropriate levels of care. My responsibilities include conducting assessments, coordinating referrals, facilitating Child and Family Team (CFT) meetings, assisting families with treatment planning, and supporting individuals through complex behavioral health challenges. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals in distress, identify service needs, and guide families through the treatment process with empathy and professionalism.

I also bring experience working within Arizona’s behavioral health system, including coordinating services with Medicaid-funded programs, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, and collaborating with multidisciplinary treatment teams. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and clear communication when helping individuals access mental health and substance use treatment.

As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am able to support diverse populations and help reduce language barriers that may prevent individuals and families from accessing care. I hold a Master of Business Administration (MBA) and a Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA), and I am currently completing my Master’s degree in Addiction Psychology at Arizona State University. This combination of clinical knowledge and administrative education allows me to approach admissions coordination with both compassion and operational efficiency.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to serve as a supportive first point of contact for adolescents, adults, and families during challenging moments. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be overwhelming, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, dignity, and reassurance.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, dedication, and commitment to accessible behavioral healthcare to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications align with the needs of your programs.

Sincerely, 
Leslie Bright

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over three years of hands-on experience in adolescent behavioral health and substance use treatment, combined with a strong background in customer service, operations, and remote team leadership, I bring a unique combination of industry knowledge, organizational skills, and compassionate communication to this opportunity.

In my current role at The Bougainvilla House, I serve as the first point of contact for families seeking mental health and substance use services. I independently manage initial inquiries, conduct pre-screenings, coordinate intake appointments, facilitate insurance benefit verification, and guide families through the admissions process. I also developed and maintain our centralized waitlist tracking system, ensuring accurate documentation, timely follow-ups, and efficient coordination with our clinical team.

Additionally, I am currently learning Kipu in preparation for my facility's transition to the platform in November. This opportunity is allowing me to expand my knowledge of behavioral health electronic medical record systems and further strengthen my technical skills within the admissions process.

Beyond my healthcare experience, I previously supervised a remote team of 15–20 representatives, developing strong skills in independent time management, team collaboration, problem-solving, and handling sensitive conversations in high-volume environments. I understand the importance of balancing efficiency with empathy, particularly when supporting adolescents and families navigating challenging circumstances.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it closely aligns with the work I find most meaningful: helping families take the first steps toward receiving appropriate mental health care. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and growing technical expertise to the admissions team at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Anjelina Deonarain

Hello,

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role. I interviewed with Devanne Bourcier in early October for a position at the Kendall site, and she mentioned admissions might be the right fit for my background. I think she was right.

At Evolutions Treatment Center, a detox and residential program for adults with substance use and co-occurring disorders, I was the first point of contact for new admissions: screening, consents, insurance and coordination of benefits, intake paperwork, and the clinical handoff, all documented in Sunwave EHR. I was promoted to Case Manager within two months and trained the intake staff who came after me. That work maps directly onto both AWA and PRC.

Before behavioral health, I managed a pipeline of inbound leads at Tesla from first inquiry to delivery and finished among the region’s top performers, with most sales coming from referrals. Before that, I spent fifteen years as a founder running my own pipeline without daily direction, which is how I work best.

I’m bilingual in English and Spanish, and I’ve been in recovery for nearly six years. I know what the first call feels like from the other side, and I know how to meet a parent there with calm, clarity, and a next step.

Thank you for your consideration.

Alex Rojas

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinical Intake Specialist position. With a Master of Social Work degree and experience providing clinical services across outpatient, emergency department, and school-based settings, I bring a strong foundation in clinical assessment, risk evaluation, crisis intervention, and care coordination.

Throughout my clinical experience, I have conducted psychosocial and mental health assessments, evaluated suicide and self-harm risk, developed individualized safety plans, and identified appropriate treatment recommendations and referrals. My experience in the emergency department strengthened my ability to assess presenting concerns, recognize immediate safety needs, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to facilitate appropriate dispositions and continuity of care. In outpatient and school-based settings, I have further developed my ability to identify clinical needs, understand complex psychosocial factors, and support individuals and families in accessing appropriate services.

I am particularly interested in this position because it aligns with my strengths in clinical assessment, gathering relevant psychosocial information, determining service needs, and helping individuals navigate the treatment process. I understand the importance of conducting thorough, compassionate, and clinically informed intakes while ensuring that safety concerns are appropriately addressed and clients are connected with suitable levels of care.

In addition to my assessment and crisis intervention experience, I bring strong communication, documentation, and interdisciplinary collaboration skills. I am comfortable working with diverse populations, including children, adolescents, adults, and families, and approach each interaction with professionalism, empathy, and sound clinical judgment.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, assessment skills, and commitment to quality mental health care would contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Shannon Beaton

candidates.cover_letter:
To whom it may concern,
My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. I've also become comfortable with higher levels of care, which I am able to use to offer clients validation and unconditional positive regard, as these experiences can be exhausting. In my current outpatient work, I primarily work with pre-teens and adolescents, as I witnessed a gap in care for these age groups despite the intensity of these transformative years. I aspire to be a supportive resource to these clients in whatever capacity I am able to, as it is already difficult to be a teen, let alone one who feels misunderstood and alone in the journey.
